prompt: What is Solstice and When Does It Occur? A solstice is a day, when the sun shines vertically over a Tropic (both cancer and Capricorn) in the afternoon and the day is the longest in that hemisphere. On the twenty-second of December, the rays of the sun fall directly over the Tropic of Capricorn. This is the longest day in Southern Hemisphere (summer season), while in the Northern Hemisphere, it is the shortest day (winter season). This is called 'Winter Solstice. On the twenty-first of June, sunlight falls vertically over the Tropic of Cancer. This is the longest day in Northern Hemisphere and hence it is called 'Summer Solstice', while in the Southern Hemisphere, it is the shortest day.
